# Study roadmap

[English](ROADMAP.md) · [中文](ROADMAP.zh.md)

Three study orders over the same problems. Pick the track that matches the role you are interviewing for and work down it. ★ shows how often a question comes up, from ★★★★★ (again and again) to ★☆☆☆☆ (rarely).

## Research track (RS / RE)

Every problem tagged RS or RE, ordered by priority and by what builds on what. ML coding comes first because it is the part that practising general algorithm problems does not cover.

### 1 · ML coding core

The three ML coding problems that come up most. They share two skills, tracing tensor shapes and differentiating matrix products.

| # | Problem | Priority | Difficulty | In one line |
| ---: | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | [Transformer Bug Hunt](coding/transformer-bug-hunt/README.md) | ★★★★☆ | Medium | A small Transformer and training script that almost work. Find the handful of planted bugs so the loss converges, then extend the model with a classification head or a KV cache. |
| 2 | [NumPy 1-NN as an Affine Layer](coding/numpy-1nn-affine/README.md) | ★★★★☆ | Medium | Write 1-nearest-neighbour classification in NumPy without Python loops, then show that the same computation is a single affine layer followed by argmax or softmax. |
| 3 | [Prefix Matmul: Autograd, Manual Backward, Hillis–Steele Scan](coding/autograd-hillis-steele/README.md) | ★★★★☆ | Hard | Prefix products of a stack of square matrices: explain why the in-place version breaks autograd, write the out-of-place forward, derive the backward by hand, then redo both passes as a parallel scan of logarithmic depth. |

### 2 · Most frequent general coding

The two most frequent coding problems overall; research roles get them too.

| # | Problem | Priority | Difficulty | In one line |
| ---: | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | [Infection Spread (Grid Cellular Automaton)](coding/infection-spread/README.md) | ★★★★★ | Medium | A grid infection spreads one step per day and every part adds a rule: immune walls, recovery after D days, neighbour thresholds and deaths. Multi-source BFS first, then a synchronous simulation. |
| 2 | [Follow Graph & Recommendations (Social Network)](coding/social-network/README.md) | ★★★★★ | Medium | Maintain who follows whom, with either time-travel queries or immutable snapshots, then recommend accounts two hops away ranked by how many of your followees already follow them. |

### 3 · Frequent, research-tagged

| # | Problem | Priority | Difficulty | In one line |
| ---: | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | [Noisy Annotators](coding/noisy-annotators/README.md) | ★★★★☆ | Medium | Training labels come from several annotators and some are unreliable. Identify them, drop or down-weight their labels, and check whether the classifier actually improves. |
| 2 | [Data Labeling Task Scheduler](coding/labeling-task-scheduler/README.md) | ★★★★☆ | Medium | Emit a list of (task, model, human) assignments so that every labeller gets at least k tasks, nobody repeats a task, and model usage per task stays balanced at every prefix of the list. |
| 3 | [Type Inference for a Toy Language](coding/type-inference/README.md) | ★★★★☆ | Medium | Types are primitives, generics and nested tuples. Print them, then infer a function's return type by unifying its generic parameters with concrete arguments and reporting conflicts. |
| 4 | [Memory Allocator](coding/memory-allocator/README.md) | ★★★★☆ | Hard | malloc and free over a fixed address range, with first-fit placement and merging of adjacent free blocks. The linear scan is only the opening move; both operations then have to come down to logarithmic time. |

### 4 · Medium frequency

Streaming Entropy reuses the log-sum-exp tools from stage 1; the restart question is pure probability.

| # | Problem | Priority | Difficulty | In one line |
| ---: | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | [Streaming Entropy](coding/streaming-entropy/README.md) | ★★★☆☆ | Medium | Entropy of softmax(logits): directly, then numerically safe, then block by block in constant extra memory, and finally a one-pass online version that rescales its accumulators when the running maximum changes. |
| 2 | [Restart Strategies under a Known Mean (Las Vegas)](coding/restart-strategy-math/README.md) | ★★★☆☆ | Hard | Only the mean latency of a request is known. Bound the tail, work out what restarts guarantee inside a time budget, find the best number of equal attempts, show when restarting cannot help, and beat equal timeouts with unequal ones. |
| 3 | [Version Dependency](coding/version-dependency/README.md) | ★★★☆☆ | Medium | Package-manager questions in four parts: find the earliest version that supports a feature with as few calls to a slow API as possible (monotone, with regressions, hierarchical bisection), then resolve dependency constraints with backtracking and a topological install order. |

### 5 · Less common, same fundamentals

| # | Problem | Priority | Difficulty | In one line |
| ---: | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | [Cross-Entropy Loss from Scratch](coding/cross-entropy-loss/README.md) | ★☆☆☆☆ | Medium | Cross-entropy on top of NumPy starter code, then masking and label smoothing, with a running conversation about the ML behind it and its link to KL divergence. |
| 2 | [Sharded Matmul: Forward, Backward, Bug Hunt](coding/sharded-matmul-backprop/README.md) | ★☆☆☆☆ | Hard | Derive and implement forward and backward for a matrix multiply whose operands are split across devices, then track down several planted bugs by tracing shapes. |
| 3 | [PyTorch Code Reading & Extension](coding/pytorch-code-reading/README.md) | ★☆☆☆☆ | — | A long, untidy PyTorch training script for a classifier with noisy annotators; answer time and memory questions about the existing code, extend it, then vectorise its slowest function. |

### 6 · ML design, deep dive and behavioral

Start the deep dive and the hiring-manager round early. Both are ★★★★★, and a story that survives follow-up questions takes longer to prepare than a coding problem.

| # | Problem | Priority | Difficulty | In one line |
| ---: | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | [ChatGPT Enterprise: RAG over Company Data](system-design/chatgpt-enterprise-rag/README.md) | ★☆☆☆☆ | — | Companies upload internal documents and get an assistant grounded in them: ingestion, chunking and embedding, retrieval and ranking, permissions, evaluation and freshness. |
| 2 | [Search & RAG ML Design (spoken)](system-design/rag-search-ml-design/README.md) | ★★☆☆☆ | — | A spoken ML design round on search: training a text embedding model contrastively (loss, positives and negatives, batch size), combining dense and lexical retrieval, reranking, and offline and online evaluation. |
| 3 | [Technical Deep Dive (with slides)](behavioral/technical-deep-dive/README.md) | ★★★★★ | — | Present one past project from slides and defend every decision: architecture, trade-offs, measured impact, what you would change, and “why not X”. |
| 4 | [Hiring Manager Round: Why OpenAI, Safety, AGI](behavioral/hiring-manager-why-openai/README.md) | ★★★★★ | — | The hiring-manager conversation: why this company and this team, your views on AGI and safety, a safety-versus-deadline dilemma, stories about ownership, conflict and failure, and working with non-engineering partners. |
| 5 | [Recruiter / HR Screen](behavioral/recruiter-screen/README.md) | ★★★★☆ | — | A walk through your background, motivation and preferred kind of work, a leadership and a conflict story, plus logistics: compensation expectations, start date, other processes, location and visa, references. |

| 22 | [Three-Card Hands and Folding](coding/poker-hands/README.md) | ★★★☆☆ | Medium | Three-card poker hands ranked by a fixed hand-type and tie-break order across many players, extended with a flush type and then with a per-player fold rule after the second card that can end play with a walkover or a stalemate before any showdown. |

| 24 | [Cloud IDE](system-design/cloud-ide/README.md) | ★★★☆☆ | Hard | A browser IDE in the style of Replit or Codespaces: per-user sandboxes, workspace lifecycle, file storage and streamed terminal output, with isolation and reconnects as the hard parts. |

| 32 | [URL Shortener](system-design/url-shortener/README.md) | ★★☆☆☆ | — | Turn long URLs into short codes and redirect them: code length and random generation, custom aliases, per-owner dedup, a cached multi-region redirect path, and approximate click counts. |

| 37 | [cd Command / Path Resolution](coding/cd-command/README.md) | ★☆☆☆☆ | Medium | Work out where `cd` lands you: normalise relative paths, add absolute paths and `~`, resolve symbolic links with cycle detection, and discuss why `cd` has to be a shell built-in. |

Evaluate on demand with cycle detection first, then keep values fresh eagerly through a dependency graph so that reads become constant time. |
| 39 | [ModalLock and FairModalLock](coding/modal-lock/README.md) | ★☆☆☆☆ | Hard | A lock that many threads may hold together as long as they ask for the same mode, then a fair version that serves waiting modes in arrival order so that none of them starves. |
| 40 | [Resumable Iterators (1D, 2D, Arbitrary Depth)](coding/resumable-iterator/README.md) | ★☆☆☆☆ | Medium | Iterators that can hand out their position and later be restored to it: an abstract interface, a flat list, a list of lists with empty rows, then nesting of any depth. |
| 41 | [In-Memory SQL-like Database](coding/in-memory-database/README.md) | ★☆☆☆☆ | Medium | An in-memory table store driven by method calls: create and insert with column projection, WHERE as AND-ed comparisons, ORDER BY over several columns each with its own direction, then hash and sorted indexes that must return exactly what a full scan would. |
| 42 | [Time-Travel Key-Value Store](coding/time-based-kv-store/README.md) | ★☆☆☆☆ | Medium | Keep several timestamped values per key and answer “what was the value at time t” with binary search; then make it testable with an injected clock, keep each key's timestamps strictly increasing, and make it thread-safe. |
| 43 | [Rate Limiter Bug Hunt](coding/rate-limiter-debug/README.md) | ★☆☆☆☆ | Medium | A per-user rate limiter with three tiers (per minute, per hour, per day) that looks like it works and passes its one happy-path test, but has four real bugs; find each one, pin it down with a test, and fix it without rewriting the class. |
| 44 | [Scheduling Agent Tool Calls with Dependencies](coding/agent-tool-scheduler/README.md) | ★☆☆☆☆ | Medium | Schedule every agent's dependent tool calls under a concurrency cap, escalating from one agent's own cap, to independent per-agent caps, to one cap shared by all agents, with a deterministic tie-break and an event-driven simulator instead of a per-tick scan. |
